content:
The test image shows a soybean leaf with dark brown/reddish-brown irregular lesions on the upper surface, somewhat coalescing. The leaf is otherwise green. This is a leaf disease.

Top candidates: Septoria_brown_spot (irregular dark brown coalescing lesions), Bacterial_Blight (angular brown lesions), Frogeye_leaf_spot (gray center with red-brown border).

Let me view one reference image.

The Septoria_brown_spot reference shows more advanced stage with yellowing and small dark spots on yellowing leaves. The test image shows large irregular dark brown/reddish coalescing lesions on a green leaf.

Reassessing: The test image lesions are large, irregular, dark brown, coalescing — no gray center, no yellow halo, no angular pattern. The leaf is from the lower canopy (on the ground). Septoria brown spot describes "irregularly shaped dark brown lesions that coalesce into larger irregular blotches, starting in lower canopy" — this matches well, even if the reference showed a more advanced yellowing stage. The early lesions before yellowing would appear as dark brown blotches on green tissue.

Septoria brown spot causes irregularly shaped dark brown lesions that merge into larger blotches, starting in the lower canopy. No gray centers (against frogeye), no angular shape or yellow halo (against bacterial blight), no reddish-purple bronzing (against cercospora)."}
